body:
I tested DIN/ISO Cycle 202 on the iTNC 530 programming station with NC software `606425 004 SP20`. I wrote a 25-line test program for the station. The program used millimeters, the G17 plane, and a separate `M99` call at each of five hole centers.

| Q214 | Q336 (degrees) | Import and Test Run |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| 0 | 0 | Passed |
| 1 | 90 | Passed |
| 2 | 180 | Passed |
| 3 | 270 | Passed |
| 4 | 45 | Passed |

The station returned all 816 bytes unchanged. For example, it accepted this definition and call:

```text
N100 G202 Q200=+2 Q201=-3 Q206=+60 Q211=+0 Q208=+60 Q203=+0 Q204=+5 Q214=+1 Q336=+90*
N110 G00 X+20 Y+15 M99*
```

Test Run displayed five holes. The log for `AAA2886.I` recorded `SIMUEND` and `STOP REASON: block END PGM or M02`. It recorded no numbered alarm during the run.

I also imported a separate program with `Q214=+5`. The converter returned exit code zero, but the readback marked the G202 block with `ERROR =`. I did not run this program.

This verifies the cycle syntax and simulated calls for this NC version. The run log contains no axis positions or spindle angles during disengagement. The display shows the holes. It gives no measurement of the shift direction, shift distance, or spindle angle. The physical Fehlmann and the CamCraft post still require separate checks. CamCraft must map the requested shift to the correct code or refuse it. The documented direction codes are in section 3.5 of the [Heidenhain cycle manual](https://content.heidenhain.de/doku/tnc_guide/pdf_files/iTNC530/60642x-04_SP8/zyklen/670388-25.pdf).
